\section{Related Work}
\label{sec:related}

\paragraph{Compound compression.}
Combining multiple compression axes produces non-additive errors.
\cite{spark-aaai2026} report super-additive degradation when combining channel pruning with token eviction; \cite{slim-icml2025} formalize compound error for quantization and sparsity.
\cite{unicomp-2026} evaluate compound compression across 40+ benchmarks, revealing that reasoning capabilities degrade disproportionately.
\cite{phase-transition-compression-2026} characterize independent phase transition points per compression dimension, implying the joint safe region is the intersection of per-dimension safe zones.
GRASPrune~\cite{graspune-acl2026} learns global budget-constrained gates for joint pruning but treats decisions as static across generation.
PM-KVQ~\cite{pmkvq-iclr2026} demonstrates that progressive quantization---gradually reducing bit-width over the generation process---mitigates cumulative error in long-CoT reasoning, implicitly introducing a temporal dimension to compression severity that resonates with our finding that compound interaction is phase-dependent.

\cite{kim2026pqqp} show that compression order (prune-then-quantize vs.\ quantize-then-prune) significantly affects joint quality, and their Progressive Intensity Hypothesis---that weaker perturbations should precede stronger ones---echoes our dose-response finding that interaction severity increases monotonically with sparsity.

These works establish compound interaction but share an implicit assumption: interaction magnitude is constant across the generation process.

\paragraph{KV cache eviction.}
StreamingLLM~\cite{streamingllm-iclr2024} establishes attention sinks as a foundational mechanism; DuoAttention~\cite{duoattention-2024} classifies heads into retrieval and streaming types, complementing our analysis of importance discrimination collapse (\S\ref{sec:discrimination-collapse-main}). Subsequent work improves eviction through per-head adaptive budgets \cite{adakv-neurips2025}, observation-window compression \cite{snapkv-neurips2024}, proxy-token strategies \cite{nacl-acl2024}, deferred importance \cite{retentivekv-2026}, and worst-case analysis \cite{defensivekv-iclr2026}; \cite{greedy-bias-kvcache-2026} show that single importance metrics exhibit systematic greedy bias. \cite{hies-2025} independently show that importance discrimination collapses under heavy single-axis pruning; our results extend this to the compound setting, revealing phase-modulated amplification and a strategy crossover (\S\ref{sec:crossover}) absent in single-axis analysis.
Recent approaches target reasoning-aware eviction \cite{rlkv-2025, longflow-2026, dong2026foresightkv}, temporal adaptivity \cite{lethe-aaai2026}, channel-level pruning \cite{xu2025think, spark-aaai2026}, and learned budgets \cite{lkv-2026}. Concurrent work~\citep{hold-onto-thought-neurips2025} evaluates single-axis compression on mathematical reasoning; we extend to the compound setting.
These methods each optimize a single pruning axis without characterizing compound interactions.

\paragraph{Phase-aware inference.}
ThinKV~\cite{thinkv-iclr2026} applies different KV strategies per phase but without compound interaction.
\cite{decision-repr-transition-2026} find pruning sensitivity depends on ``silent'' vs.\ ``decisive'' representation phases.
\cite{doing-more-with-less-2026} show pruning combined with test-time scaling can exceed unpruned baselines; \cite{sparse-frontier-2025} find no universally optimal sparse attention strategy across generation stages.
\cite{physics-kvcache-2026} identify a sharp phase transition in single-axis KV cache compression at high sparsity, characterizing the single-dimension failure mode that our compound analysis extends across multiple axes.
R-KV~\cite{rkv-neurips2025} exploits reasoning-specific redundancy for aggressive cache compression, targeting per-axis optimization rather than characterizing compound degradation.
These works establish phase-dependent compression tolerance along single axes.
Our work bridges this by quantifying how compound severity varies across phases and eviction strategies.

\section{Introduction}
\label{sec:introduction}

Long-context language models place acute pressure on the key--value (KV) cache, which grows linearly with sequence length \cite{kwon-sosp2023, pope-mlsys2023}.
Two complementary responses---\emph{attention head pruning} \cite{voita-acl2019, michel-neurips2019} and \emph{KV cache eviction} \cite{snapkv-neurips2024, adakv-neurips2025}---can be deployed simultaneously as \emph{compound sparsity}, but the resulting quality degradation is often super-additive \cite{spark-aaai2026, slim-icml2025}. Recent evaluations confirm that reasoning capabilities degrade disproportionately under compound compression \cite{unicomp-2026}, and that per-dimension safe zones intersect to form a smaller joint safe region \cite{phase-transition-compression-2026}.

Prior work treats compound interaction magnitude as roughly constant across generation \cite{spark-aaai2026, unicomp-2026}, despite evidence that pruning sensitivity depends on representational phase \cite{decision-repr-transition-2026} and that no single sparse attention strategy dominates across generation stages \cite{sparse-frontier-2025}.
This assumption is problematic for reasoning models, whose chain-of-thought generations \cite{wei-neurips2022-cot} alternate between broadly distributed attention (exploratory reasoning) and sharply concentrated attention (structured computation) \cite{thinkv-iclr2026}.
Phase-aware methods like ThinKV \cite{thinkv-iclr2026} apply different KV strategies per phase but without considering compound interaction, while importance-based eviction itself faces challenges from greedy bias \cite{greedy-bias-kvcache-2026}, deferred importance \cite{retentivekv-2026}, and temporal dynamics in long generations \cite{lethe-aaai2026}. These methods each optimize a single pruning axis; we characterize the interaction when multiple mechanisms are composed.
If compound severity varies across these phases, a uniform sparsity budget may be safe in one phase yet destructive in another.

What does compound interaction add beyond single-axis findings? Single-axis results on score collapse \cite{hies-2025}, phase-aware eviction \cite{thinkv-iclr2026}, and strategy non-dominance \cite{sparse-frontier-2025} qualitatively predict phase-dependent compound degradation---but two quantitative patterns cannot be derived from single-axis analyses. First, the severity gradient follows a \emph{strictly monotonic dose-response} (Jonckheere-Terpstra $z{=}33.7$, $p \ll 10^{-10}$). Second, in DeepSeek a \emph{strategy ranking crossover} emerges at $s{=}0.25$; Qwen shows consistent importance dominance, indicating model dependence. We report the paired median difference $\Delta$ ($0.39 \to 8.48$) as primary and the amplification ratio $G{=}7.5$--$79.8{\times}$ as an exploratory measure (\S\ref{sec:results}).

We find that compound sparsity severity is strongly modulated by reasoning phase and eviction strategy.
Under importance-based KV cache eviction, the Interaction Index---a measure of super-additive degradation---concentrates in low-sparsity phases and is largely absent in high-sparsity phases.
On DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-7B (500 MATH-500 problems), the median phase difference rises from $0.39$ at $s{=}0.15$ to $8.48$ at $s{=}0.30$ (all Bonferroni-corrected $p \ll 10^{-10}$; Jonckheere-Terpstra $z{=}33.7$, $p \ll 10^{-10}$).
The pattern replicates on Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct ($\Delta$: $0.07 \to 3.16$; all $p < 10^{-14}$); preliminary evidence from DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Llama-8B (LlamaForCausalLM) suggests the phenomenon may extend beyond Qwen2 but at ${\sim}1/40$ the magnitude and with substantially weaker strategy contrast.
Random eviction develops a detectable but weak phase gradient only above $s \approx 0.20$ ($2.7$--$17{\times}$ smaller than importance-based where both strategies are significant, $s \geq 0.25$), confirming that the dominant gradient is an emergent phase-strategy interaction.

We present correlational evidence for \emph{importance discrimination collapse}---the degeneration of head importance scores toward uniformity under compound stress---as a contributing factor, with the \emph{structural specificity} of importance-based pruning (which selectively removes high-score heads) as a key differentiator from random pruning.

This work is a \textbf{diagnostic study}: we characterize a previously unknown interaction effect rather than proposing a mitigation method, following the tradition of empirical analysis papers \cite{voita-acl2019, michel-neurips2019}.
Our contributions:
\begin{enumerate}[nosep,leftmargin=*]
    \item We characterize a \textbf{phase--strategy interaction}: importance-based eviction exhibits a severity gradient across reasoning phases that is $2.7$--$17{\times}$ larger than under random eviction where both strategies show significant phase gradients ($s \geq 0.25$) on MATH-500; the gradient direction is consistent on GSM8K, where importance-based eviction produces significant phase gradients while random eviction does not (\S\ref{sec:cross-benchmark}).\footnote{The full MATH-500 range including non-significant random conditions ($s \leq 0.20$, where random $\Delta$ CIs span zero) extends to $39{\times}$.}
    \item We document that this gradient \textbf{increases monotonically with sparsity} and replicates across two Qwen2-architecture models with different training paradigms (DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-7B, reasoning-distilled; Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, instruction-tuned), with preliminary evidence from a LlamaForCausalLM model suggesting the phenomenon may extend beyond Qwen2 (\S\ref{sec:results}).
    \item We provide a \textbf{correlational diagnostic} showing that aggregate importance discrimination collapse (Gini) is correlated with but not sufficient for severity amplification, with the structural specificity of pruned heads as the key differentiator (\S\ref{sec:analysis}).
\end{enumerate}

The paper addresses two major challenges in deploying LLMs in streaming applications: memory consumption from caching Key and Value states of previous tokens during decoding, and the inability of LLMs to generalize to longer texts than their training sequence length.

DuoAttention applies a full KV cache only to retrieval heads while using a lightweight, constant-length KV cache for streaming heads, reducing both decoding and pre-filling memory and latency without compromising long-context abilities. **Summary of the paper:**

While current Large Language Models (LLMs) exhibit remarkable reasoning capabilities through test-time compute scaling (TTS), their massive parameter counts and high inference costs have motivated the development of pruning methods that can reduce model size without sacrificing performance.

However, prior work has shown that structured pruning (methods which removes entire set of layer blocks) significantly degrades TTS reasoning performance. In this work, the authors investigate whether unstructured pruning (methods that carefully remove only certain redundant/detrimental weights) exhibits similar limitations.

**Key findings:**

Experiments across four reasoning benchmarks on two reasoning LLMs (s1.1-7B and Qwen3-8B) consistently show that unstructured pruning augments TTS performance compared to structured pruning, and at times can even outperform the unpruned full-weight LLMs.

These findings challenge the conventional notion that pruning always reduces TTS performance and suggest that carefully undertaken pruning can improve TTS effectiveness even further.

The paper was authored by Ocean Monjur, Shahriar Kabir Nahin, and Anshuman Chhabra from the Bellini College of AI, Cybersecurity, and Computing at the University of South Florida, and was submitted on April 28, 2026.

## DefensiveKV: Taming the Fragility of KV Cache Eviction in LLM Inference

The paper is authored by Yuan Feng, Haoyu Guo, Junlin Lv, S. Kevin Zhou, and Xike Xie (arXiv:2510.13334).

### Core Problem and Contribution

Large language models face substantial memory and runtime overhead from the transformer's Key-Value cache. Recent methods employ a scoring-aggregation framework to evict unimportant cache entries, based on the stability assumption—that a fixed subset of entries remains consistently important during generation.

The paper argues that this underlying assumption is inherently fragile, making mean aggregation highly vulnerable in extreme cases. To counter this, they propose a simple yet elegant defensive aggregation strategy: a two-step, linear-time approach that controls worst-case risk, thereby defending against extreme cases with negligible computational overhead.

### Methods

The paper proposes a novel cache eviction method, DefensiveKV and its extension, Layer-DefensiveKV, which incorporates layer-wise budget allocation. The key innovation in DefensiveKV is the strategic replacement of conventional mean aggregation with defensive aggregation, which reduces over 2× in generation quality loss.

### Results

Across seven task domains (18 datasets), the methods reduce generation quality loss by 2.3× and 4.3× respectively, versus the strongest baseline under a 20% cache size. These results set new performance benchmarks and pioneer a promising direction for optimizing cache eviction against underlying fragility through worst-case risk management.

The code is available at https://github.com/FFY0/DefensiveKV.

## GRASPrune: Global Gating for Budgeted Structured Pruning

GRASPrune is a structured pruning framework applied after pretraining that jointly prunes FFN channels and KV head groups under a single global budget.

Sparse attention offers a promising strategy to extend long-context capabilities in Transformer LLMs, yet its efficiency-accuracy trade-offs remain unclear due to the lack of comprehensive evaluation.

## Overview

The paper addresses the challenge of rapid KV cache growth during long-output context generation of large reasoning models with extended chain of thought (CoT), which overwhelms GPU memory.

## Key Approach

ThinKV is a thought-adaptive KV cache compression framework based on the observation that attention sparsity reveals distinct thought types with varying importance within the CoT. 

It applies a hybrid quantization-eviction strategy, assigning token precision by thought importance and progressively evicting tokens from less critical thoughts as reasoning trajectories evolve.

## Implementation

To implement ThinKV, the authors designed a kernel that extends PagedAttention to enable efficient reuse of evicted tokens' memory slots, eliminating compaction overheads.

## Results

Extensive experiments on DeepSeek-R1-Distill, GPT-OSS, and NVIDIA AceReason across mathematics and coding benchmarks show that ThinKV achieves near-lossless accuracy with less than 5% of the original KV cache, while improving performance with up to 5.8x higher inference throughput over state-of-the-art baselines.

## Authors

The paper was authored by Akshat Ramachandran, Marina Neseem, Charbel Sakr, Rangharajan Venkatesan, Brucek Khailany, and Tushar Krishna.

The paper was posted to arXiv on October 1, 2025 (arXiv:2510.01290).
